title: Align make check stamp-file behavior with AGENTS rules
description:
The repo currently has conflicting guidance about `tmp/.check-passed`.

`AGENTS.md` explicitly says: "Never bypass enforcement hooks. Don't `touch tmp/.check-passed` to fake a passing check, don't write stamp files manually..." But `Makefile` still implements `make check` by running the checks and then unconditionally doing `touch tmp/.check-passed`. The pre-hook in `.claude/hooks/enforce-agents-rules.py` then treats that stamp file as the source of truth for whether `gh pr create` is allowed.

That leaves the repo in an awkward state where the documented rule says not to write the stamp file manually, while the canonical check target writes it manually.

Clean this up by choosing a single, coherent policy:
1. If the stamp file is the intended mechanism, update the docs/rules so `make check` is the only sanctioned writer.
2. If manual stamp files are truly banned, move the PR-precondition logic to a different source of truth and remove the `touch tmp/.check-passed` step.

Either way, the current contradiction should be resolved so the docs, Makefile, and enforcement hook all agree.
